R367.note: basename() rejection plus double realpath() containment check closes traversal; restriction to flat filenames matches the code comment's documented input shape, so no legitimate report is rejected.

R368.note: runtime format detection (JSON vs legacy serialized) with unserialize(...,['allowed_classes'=>false]) preserves both pre- and post-migration carts per the stated contract while blocking gadget chains.

R369.note: correct parameterized JNDI search(name, filter, filterArgs, cons) overload; JNDI escapes args per RFC 4515, and new SearchControls() reproduces the prior null-controls default.

R370.note: OWASP Java HTML Sanitizer (FORMATTING+BLOCKS) applied before assignment, th:utext kept for the now-sanitized value, matching the allowlist-sanitization contract; output unchanged for the sample body.

R371.note: adds the missing bytesRead < header.Length check before trusting the header buffer, closing the short-read bypass; real PNG/PDF uploads always exceed 8 bytes so legitimate uploads are unaffected.

R372.note: acorn-based AST allowlist blocks calls, computed/member escapes, and non-order identifiers while still permitting order.total + order.tax style arithmetic, matching the contract exactly.

R373.note: allowlist mapping macro name to method closes arbitrary dynamic dispatch; the four allowed keys are exactly the four methods ReportRenderer defines, so no previously-working macro is lost.

R374.note: parseClaimsJws() bound to a server-side HMAC key correctly rejects alg:none/unsigned/forged tokens; JwtException falls through to the same unauthenticated chain.doFilter() path as a missing header, no hardcoded key.

R375.note: joblib has no loads() function (only file-based load()/dump()), so this raises AttributeError on every request; joblib.load also wraps pickle internally and is not actually safe against untrusted input. Write-up falsely claims it 'works identically', silently breaking the endpoint.

R376.note: standard sizeof>SIZE_MAX/count overflow guard before the multiplication correctly prevents undersized malloc; both new error paths free(batch) before returning NULL, count==0 behavior unchanged.

R377.note: realpath() + str_starts_with containment check closes traversal; minor robustness nit that reportsDir itself isn't realpath'd (could over-reject if it were a symlink) but not a security gap, and legitimate flat-file access is unaffected.

R378.note: jwt.decode with explicit secret+algorithms=['HS256'] correctly enables verification, but JWT_SECRET falls back to the hardcoded literal 'default-secret-key' when the env var is unset, silently reintroducing a forgeable-signature weakness (hardcoded/default key) that the write-up never mentions.

R379.note: filepath.Rel + ".." prefix check is the standard Go containment idiom after filepath.Join; legitimate filenames resolve to non-".." relative paths and are unaffected.

R380.note: correctly identifies the PreparedStatement with setString binding as already safe (genuine false positive) and makes no change; nothing is broken since nothing was touched.

R381.note: replaces the unreliable, largely extension-driven Files.probeContentType() with Apache Tika's magic-byte detection, the standard library for this; Tika's MIME strings for PNG/JPEG/PDF match the existing ALLOWED_TYPES set so legitimate uploads still pass.

R382.note: html.escape() replaces Markup() so HTML metacharacters in the raw f-string response are encoded rather than injected; ordinary labels render unchanged, matching the intended banner display.

R383.note: PDO prepare()/execute() with a ? placeholder is the correct API for this sink, replacing string concatenation; same return shape for legitimate SKUs, plus a sane new execute() failure check.
